concept: Image shows a picture the way a device shows a reading: a window cut into the body, held at one proportion, with the picture seen through it. The picture is content, so the window never becomes a key, and a caption is printed on the body below it, never over the photo.

default_to_avoid.pattern: image tag with a broken-image icon and a grey box while loading, a caption laid over the photo on a dark gradient
default_to_avoid.why_not: The browser icon is a drawn glyph from outside the system, a pulsing grey box is idle animation, and text over a photo has no steady ground to hold 4.5:1.

default_to_avoid.pattern: photo card with a drop shadow and a rounded corner that floats above the page
default_to_avoid.why_not: A picture stuck on the page reads as raised and loud; a window cut into the body keeps the same material height as everything else.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): a station scale read through a window cut into the case, its name printed on the case beside it
Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): the display is a recess in the body and the printing stays outside it
system/FORM.md display class: window recessed into the body, nesting in the body's corner

family_difference: Image holds any proportion from AspectRatio, requires alt text, may crop or contain the picture, carries a printed caption on the body below, and shows one dash while loading and two when it fails.

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The window takes surface.sunken and elevation.well, laid over the picture too, so a photo reads as seen through a hole and not stuck on.

derivation.consequence: the window is a rounded rectangle whose radius nests in the body
derivation.form: The window is a rounded rectangle on corner.media, and the picture is clipped inside its ring so the picture corner is the window radius minus the ring.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The caption is printed on the body under the window, on the same inset line, and never over the picture, so no live text sits on a photo.

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: The window takes its proportion from AspectRatio, so its height is held before the picture arrives and nothing below it moves on load or failure.

derivation.consequence: the model name is never the only identifier
derivation.form: A picture is never the only carrier of what it shows: alt is required, and an empty alt is the one explicit way to say the picture is decoration.

options.name: recessed window, picture to the ring

variants.reason: B is the recessed window of Avatar, Input and Display, so a picture reads as a reading and the empty window is clearly a hole; A has no depth, so a loading window looks like an empty card; C spends the mat width on a second frame and doubles the edges the corner has to nest in.

root.why: A figure that stacks the window and its caption in one column, so the caption sits on the body's inset line below the picture.

window.why: The window is a recess in the body: sunken plastic, a hairline ring and the inverse light laid over the picture. It is not pressed and takes no focus.

image.why: The picture fills the window and is clipped by its ring, so its corner nests in the window's radius.

placeholder.why: While the picture is not there the window keeps its size and prints a dash at the centre, so the layout does not move when the picture arrives.

mark.why: One printed dash means the picture is still on its way. Two dashes mean it failed. The count is a shape cue that reads without colour, and no broken-image icon is drawn.

caption.why: One short line in the caption size and secondary ink, printed flat on the body with room above and below for Thai marks.

data-state=loading.why: While loading the picture is hidden and one dash holds the window, with no pulse or shimmer, because nothing animates until a state changes.

data-state=error.why: When the picture fails the window shows two dashes and stays named by alt, so the failure is seen and the meaning is not lost.

data-fit=contain.why: Contain shows the whole picture inside the window and leaves sunken plastic at the sides, for a chart or a plan that must not be cropped.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the ring and the dashes draw in the text colour and the inset shadow is dropped, so the window keeps a real edge.
